editorial.titleTr: Presidential Constitutional Revision Push Rings Hollow Without Term Limit Renunciation Declaration
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung emphasized the need for constitutional reform but did not declare an end to presidential reelection eligibility.
Sixty-three percent of the public wants constitutional amendments to prohibit presidential reelection.
The authenticity of constitutional reform discussions has emerged as a key point of contention.

summaryTr: Seoul Police Agency transferred the bribery allegations against Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won to the Yeongdeungpo Police Station.
An editorial criticizes the police's lack of investigative will and points out that this is a grave matter.
It urges the prosecution to launch a reinvestigation to clarify the truth.
editorial.bodyTr: The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency has transferred the case involving bribery and favor-seeking allegations against Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won to the Yeongdeungpo Police Station. editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Ignoring Electoral Law Leaves Door Open for More Satellite Party Parasites Like Yong Hye-in
summaryTr: The presidential office maintains its nomination of the controversial ministerial candidate and will proceed with the confirmation hearing.
The mixed-member proportional electoral system leads to a proliferation of satellite parties and favoritism toward proportional representatives.
Fundamental electoral law reform is essential to block political maneuvering.
editorials.bodyTr: The presidential office has decided to maintain its nomination of controversial minister candidates and announced plans to proceed with confirmation hearings. Some are pointing out that the current semi-proportional electoral system is a structural cause of satellite party proliferation and preferential treatment for proportional representatives, emphasizing the need to abolish the system and undertake fundamental electoral law reforms to prevent political maneuvering.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: If You Won't Enforce 'Zombie University' Crackdown, Why Pass the Law?
summaryTr: The Private University Structural Improvement Act has been implemented, but the Education Ministry is responding lukewarmly.
As the elimination of poorly-run universities is delayed, student damages are mounting.

This editorial criticizes the current situation and urges the government to promptly enforce administrative measures to minimize harm to students.

editorial.body: 입력 김승원 법무부 장관 후보자가 코로나19 치료제 임상시험 승인 청탁 의혹에 대해 “민원 전달 과정에서 더욱 신중하게 해야 했다”면서도 “부정한 청탁을 한 적이 없다”고 말했다. 자신이 식약처장에게 전화를 걸고 문자를 보낸 사실을 “민원 전달”이라고 표현하며 문제될 일이 아니라는 뜻을 밝힌 것으로 들린다. 지금 공개된 녹취로 드러난 김 후보자의 청탁 전후 언행을 놓고 공직자로서의 적격 여부를 문제 삼으며 여론이 들끓고 있는 것과는 천양지차의 안일한 인식이다. 김 후보자는 “승인되는 순간 수천억원을 벌 수 있는 거”라고 말했다. “승원 오빠가 식약처장에게다 얘기하고 오늘 또 ‘보건복지부에 푸시해 줄까’라고 그랬다”는 청탁 브로커 양씨의 녹취도 나왔다. 이쯤 되면 일의 앞뒤가 짐작되고도 남는데도, 김 후보자가 ‘공익 민원’이라고까지 강변하고 있으니 국민의 상식과 법 감정에 정면으로 반한다. 김 후보자는 자신의 결백을 주장하면서 “식약처의 심사가 공정하게 이뤄지지 않은 것도 아니다”는 점을 들었는데 이 역시 인식의 왜곡이다. 국민이 문제 삼는 것은 적절치 못한 청탁성 민원 그 자체에 있는 것이지, 민원의 결과를 묻고 있는 것이 아니다. 위법은 행위의 순간에 성립되는 것이지 성공 여부에 따라 가려지는 게 아님은 법조인 출신인 김 후보자가 누구보다도 잘 알 터이다. 더구나 김 의원의 청탁이 얼마나 작용했는지는 지금 알 수 없지만, 해당 업체는 실제로 임상시험 승인을 받았다. 법무부 장관은 법 질서를 확립해야 하는 자리다. 그런 만큼 잣대의 공정성이 무엇보다 중요하다. 그런데 정작 장관 후보자가 공과 사를 구분하지 못하고 사적 이권을 위해 지위를 이용한 정황이 드러나고 있다. 김 후보자에게 임상시험 승인을 청탁한 브로커는 해당 기업 대표로부터 거액을 투자받은 사실까지 확인됐다. 임상시험 승인 전후로 미공개 정보를 이용한 주식 거래 등 다양한 형태의 불법 행위가 이뤄져 일반투자자들의 피해도 발생했다. 이런 일과 관련해 부정 청탁 의혹이 제기되는 후보자에게, 더구나 자신이 한 일에 대한 사과는커녕 대수롭지 않다는 투로 말하는 사람에게 법치주의의 수호라는 중책을 맡길 수 있겠는가.

editorial.titleTr: Ex-Justice Minister Nominee Claims Improper Favor Request Was Public Interest Petition
summaryTr: Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won claims clinical trial approval request was 'public interest petition'
Recorded conversation reveals mention of hundreds of billions in profits, involvement of bribery brokers and other damaging circumstances
Legal expert's inability to distinguish public from private affairs and abuse of position raises questions about qualifications to uphold rule of law
editorial.bodyTr:
Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won said he should have been "more cautious in the process of conveying civil complaints" regarding allegations of soliciting approval for a COVID-19 treatment drug clinical trial, but claimed he "never made improper solicitations." By describing his phone calls and text messages to the head of the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety as a "civil complaint delivery," he appears to be suggesting there is nothing problematic about his actions. This complacent perception stands in stark contrast to the current public outcry questioning his qualifications as a public official based on his words and actions before and after the alleged solicitation, as revealed in the recently released recordings.

Kim said, "The moment it gets approved, you can make hundreds of billions of won." A recording also emerged of broker Yang, who allegedly brokered the solicitation, saying, "Seung-won oppa talked to the head of the Food and Drug Safety Ministry, and today he said, 'Should I push this to the Ministry of Health and Welfare too?'" Given this sequence of events, one can well infer what happened. Yet Kim continues to insist this was a "public interest civil complaint," directly contradicting the common sense and legal sensibilities of the public. Kim argued his innocence by stating that "the Food and Drug Safety Ministry's review was conducted fairly," but this too reflects a distorted understanding. What the public takes issue with is the inappropriate nature of the solicitation-like complaint itself, not the outcome of the complaint. As someone with a legal background, Kim should know better than anyone that wrongdoing is established at the moment of the act, not determined by whether it succeeds or fails. Moreover, while we cannot yet determine how much influence Kim's solicitation had, the company in question did actually receive approval for the clinical trial. The Minister of Justice is tasked with establishing the rule of law, making impartiality of standards paramount. Yet the nominee himself is showing signs of failing to distinguish between public and private interests and abusing his position for personal gain. The broker who solicited Kim for clinical trial approval was confirmed to have received substantial investments from the company's representative. Various forms of illegal activity—including stock trading based on non-public information before and after the clinical trial approval—took place, causing losses to ordinary investors. Can we entrust the protection of the rule of law to a nominee facing allegations of improper solicitation in connection with such activities, especially one who shows no remorse for his actions and dismisses them as trivial?

editorial.title: Demographic gravity
editorial.body: Korea needs comprehensive reforms across labor, welfare, fiscal policy for hyper-aging The world has crossed a demographic threshold that no amount of fiscal tinkering can reverse. Adults aged 65 and older now outnumber children under 5 worldwide for the first time, according to the US Census Bureau. While this structural pivot affects every major economy, South Korea is accelerating through it faster than any other nation. The country entered the super-aged category in late 2024, when seniors reached 20 percent of the population. Their share rose to 20.3 percent in 2025 and is projected to reach 41 percent by 2060, the highest in the world. Over the same period, the median age would climb from 46 to 59.2, while the population itself would fall from 52.19 million to 46.95 million. Japan, currently older, is projected to reach 38.8 percent, leaving Korea with a demographic profile unlike any major economy. The more revealing number is the old-age dependency ratio. It stood at 29.5 elderly people for every 100 working-age adults last year. By 2060, it is expected to hit 81.6, leaving roughly 1.2 working-age people for each senior. That forecast should change the policy conversation. Population aging cannot be handled as another short-term demographic emergency. The nation has to redesign institutions for a society with fewer workers, longer lives and far greater demand for pensions and care. Start with childbirth. Seoul has spent heavily on parental allowances, housing support and other incentives, yet the basic economics of raising a child remain difficult. Expensive housing, fierce competition for educational credentials and costly private tutoring all weigh on family formation. Family policy also needs to catch up with social reality. Support should reach households raising children outside traditional marriage, including cohabiting couples. The second adjustment concerns productivity. A shrinking workforce does not automatically dictate a shrinking economy. Scarcer labor can make investment in machinery, robotics and artificial intelligence more attractive, allowing output to rise even as the number of workers falls. Korea, already strong in advanced manufacturing, has an unusual opportunity to make technology part of its demographic response. The country should measure success by output per worker rather than the size of the workforce. Its labor market needs updating alongside its factories. Seniority-based pay encourages earlier retirement by making experienced workers progressively more expensive. Greater use of task-based and performance-based pay could keep older workers economically active while giving younger employees more flexible entry points. Another challenge is Korea’s elderly poverty rate, which stood at 40.5 percent in 2020, the highest among OECD members, although the OECD has more recently estimated it at 39.7 percent. The late introduction of the national pension, limited coverage and low benefits help explain the gap. Meanwhile, longer lives will increase demand for health and long-term care. The Health and Welfare Ministry estimates that 10.34 percent of Koreans aged 65 and over could have dementia by 2040. Care systems that rely heavily on unpaid family labor will become harder to sustain as families themselves become smaller. This is a fiscal issue as much as a medical one. Some senior benefits may eventually need an age threshold above 65, which has remained unchanged since 1981. But fiscal adjustment should be paired with stronger protection for poor elderly people. A higher eligibility age cannot become a convenient way to move costs onto those least able to bear them. Managing hyper-aging requires a dual commitment: easing the structural economic pressures that deter young adults from starting families while re-engineering labor, fiscal and care frameworks for an older population. Demographic change offers no room for political bargaining. Korea’s economic viability hinges on how decisively its leadership transforms institutions to match this permanent reality. editorial.bodyTr: 세계는 재정적 미봉책으로도 되돌릴 수 없는 인구통계적 임계점을 넘었다. 미국 인구조사국에 따르면 65세 이상의 성인이 5세 미만의 아동보다 많아진 것이 전 세계적으로 처음이다. 이러한 구조적 변화는 모든 주요 경제국에 영향을 미치지만, 대한민국은 다른 어느 국가보다 빠른 속도로 진행되고 있다. 한국은 2024년 말 노년층이 인구의 20%에 도달하면서 초고령사회에 진입했다. 2025년에는 20.3%로 상승했으며 2060년에는 41%에 도달할 것으로 예상되는데, 이는 세계에서 가장 높은 수치다. 같은 기간 중위 나이는 46세에서 59.2세로 올라가고, 인구는 5,219만 명에서 4,695만 명으로 감소할 것이다. 현재 더 고령화된 일본은 38.8%에 도달할 것으로 예상되어, 한국은 주요 경제국 중 어디와도 다른 인구통계적 프로필을 갖게 될 것이다. 더욱 주목할 만한 수치는 노년부양비다. 지난해 경제활동인구 100명당 65세 이상 노년층이 29.5명이었다. 2060년에는 81.6명에 도달하여 각 노인 1명당 경제활동인구가 약 1.2명으로 줄어들 것으로 예상된다. 이러한 전망은 정책 논의를 바꿔야 한다. 인구 고령화는 또 다른 단기적 인구통계 위기로 취급될 수 없다. 국가는 더 적은 노동력, 더 긴 수명, 그리고 연금과 돌봄에 대한 훨씬 더 큰 수요를 가진 사회를 위해 제도를 재설계해야 한다. 출산부터 시작하자. 서울은 양육 수당, 주택 지원, 기타 인센티브에 많은 돈을 썼지만, 아이를 양육하는 데 드는 기본 경제는 여전히 어렵다. 비싼 주택, 학력에 대한 치열한 경쟁, 비용이 많이 드는 사교육이 모두 가족 형성에 영향을 미친다. 가족 정책도 사회적 현실을 따라잡아야 한다. 지원은 동거 커플을 포함한 전통적 결혼 외의 형태로 자녀를 키우는 가구에까지 확대되어야 한다. 두 번째 조정은 생산성에 관한 것이다. 축소되는 노동력이 반드시 축소되는 경제를 의미하지는 않는다. 노동력이 부족하면 기계, 로봇 공학, 인공지능에 대한 투자가 더욱 매력적이 되어 근로자 수가 줄어들어도 생산량이 증가할 수 있다. 이미 첨단 제조업에 강한 한국은 기술을 인구통계적 대응의 일부로 만들 수 있는 드문 기회를 가지고 있다. 국가는 노동력의 규모가 아닌 근로자당 생산량으로 성공을 측정해야 한다. 노동시장도 공장과 함께 현대화되어야 한다. 연공서열 임금은 경험 많은 근로자를 점점 더 비싸지게 만들어 조기 퇴직을 조장한다. 과제 기반 및 성과 기반 임금의 확대 활용은 노년층 근로자를 경제 활동에 유지시키면서 젊은 직원들에게 더 유연한 진입 기회를 제공할 수 있다. 또 다른 도전은 한국의 노인 빈곤율로, 2020년에 40.5%로 OECD 회원국 중 가장 높았으며, 비록 OECD는 최근에 이를 39.7%로 추정했다. 국민연금의 늦은 도입, 제한적 보장 범위, 낮은 급여가 이러한 격차를 설명하는 데 도움이 된다. 한편, 더 긴 수명은 건강 및 장기요양 돌봄에 대한 수요를 증가시킬 것이다. 보건복지부는 2040년까지 65세 이상의 한국인 중 10.34%가 치매를 앓을 수 있다고 추정한다. 무급 가족 노동에 크게 의존하는 돌봄 체계는 가족 자체가 작아지면서 지속하기 어려워질 것이다. 이것은 의료 문제만큼 재정 문제이기도 하다. 일부 노인 급여는 결국 1981년부터 변하지 않은 65세 이상의 연령 기준이 필요할 수도 있다. 그러나 재정 조정은 빈곤한 노인에 대한 강화된 보호와 함께 이루어져야 한다. 더 높은 적격 나이가 감당할 수 없는 사람들에게 비용을 전가하는 편리한 방법이 되어서는 안 된다. 초고령화 관리는 이중 약속을 필요로 한다. 젊은 성인들이 가족을 시작하는 것을 막는 구조적 경제 압력을 완화하는 동시에 고령 인구를 위해 노동, 재정, 돌봄 체계를 재설계하는 것이다. 인구통계적 변화는 정치적 협상의 여지가 없다. 한국의 경제적 생존력은 지도부가 이 영구적인 현실에 맞게 얼마나 단호하게 제도를 변혁하는지에 달려 있다.

editorials.title: Demographic gravity
editorials.body: Korea needs comprehensive reforms across labor, welfare, fiscal policy for hyper-aging The world has crossed a demographic threshold that no amount of fiscal tinkering can reverse. Adults aged 65 and older now outnumber children under 5 worldwide for the first time, according to the US Census Bureau. While this structural pivot affects every major economy, South Korea is accelerating through it faster than any other nation. The country entered the super-aged category in late 2024, when seniors reached 20 percent of the population. Their share rose to 20.3 percent in 2025 and is projected to reach 41 percent by 2060, the highest in the world. Over the same period, the median age would climb from 46 to 59.2, while the population itself would fall from 52.19 million to 46.95 million. Japan, currently older, is projected to reach 38.8 percent, leaving Korea with a demographic profile unlike any major economy. The more revealing number is the old-age dependency ratio. It stood at 29.5 elderly people for every 100 working-age adults last year. By 2060, it is expected to hit 81.6, leaving roughly 1.2 working-age people for each senior. That forecast should change the policy conversation. Population aging cannot be handled as another short-term demographic emergency. The nation has to redesign institutions for a society with fewer workers, longer lives and far greater demand for pensions and care. Start with childbirth. Seoul has spent heavily on parental allowances, housing support and other incentives, yet the basic economics of raising a child remain difficult. Expensive housing, fierce competition for educational credentials and costly private tutoring all weigh on family formation. Family policy also needs to catch up with social reality. Support should reach households raising children outside traditional marriage, including cohabiting couples. The second adjustment concerns productivity. A shrinking workforce does not automatically dictate a shrinking economy. Scarcer labor can make investment in machinery, robotics and artificial intelligence more attractive, allowing output to rise even as the number of workers falls. Korea, already strong in advanced manufacturing, has an unusual opportunity to make technology part of its demographic response. The country should measure success by output per worker rather than the size of the workforce. Its labor market needs updating alongside its factories. Seniority-based pay encourages earlier retirement by making experienced workers progressively more expensive. Greater use of task-based and performance-based pay could keep older workers economically active while giving younger employees more flexible entry points. Another challenge is Korea’s elderly poverty rate, which stood at 40.5 percent in 2020, the highest among OECD members, although the OECD has more recently estimated it at 39.7 percent. The late introduction of the national pension, limited coverage and low benefits help explain the gap. Meanwhile, longer lives will increase demand for health and long-term care. The Health and Welfare Ministry estimates that 10.34 percent of Koreans aged 65 and over could have dementia by 2040. Care systems that rely heavily on unpaid family labor will become harder to sustain as families themselves become smaller. This is a fiscal issue as much as a medical one. Some senior benefits may eventually need an age threshold above 65, which has remained unchanged since 1981. But fiscal adjustment should be paired with stronger protection for poor elderly people. A higher eligibility age cannot become a convenient way to move costs onto those least able to bear them. Managing hyper-aging requires a dual commitment: easing the structural economic pressures that deter young adults from starting families while re-engineering labor, fiscal and care frameworks for an older population. Demographic change offers no room for political bargaining. Korea’s economic viability hinges on how decisively its leadership transforms institutions to match this permanent reality. editorial.body: 경찰이 지난 7일 더불어민주당 원내대표를 지낸 김병기 무소속 의원에 대해 수사 착수 1년 만에 구속영장을 신청했다. 구속영장은 범죄 혐의가 소명된 피의자가 ‘도주나 증거 인멸 우려가 있을 때’ 구속하기 위한 것이다. 김 의원이 증거를 없앨 우려가 있다면 진작에 구속했어
editorial.pullQuote: 김 의원이 증거를 없앨 우려가 있다면 진작에 구속했어야 한다.
summary: 경찰이 김병기 의원 수사 1년 만에 구속영장을 신청했다.
